newsitem.title: GERMANY: TENNIS-SPAIN WIN WORLD TEAM CUP.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-SPAIN WIN WORLD TEAM CUP.

text.p: Albert Costa and Felix Mantilla enjoyed singles victories to lead Spain to a 2-0 win over Australia in the final of the $1.9-million World Team Cup on Sunday.
Mantilla beat Mark Woodforde 7-5 6-2 while Costa overcame Mark Philippoussis 3-6 7-6 7-6 to give Spain their fourth title, equalling the record held by the United States.
The pivotal match of the tie was between hard-serving Philippoussis and Costa, who had not dropped a set all week.
Philippoussis won the first set in emphatic fashion, blasting a world record 229-kph ace past Costa. The ace bettered Philippoussis's own mark of 228.5 kph set in March in Scottsdale, Arizona.
But the tough-as-nails Spaniard came back to take the next two sets on tie-breaks.
Mantilla, ranked 11 in the world, had given Spain a 1-0 lead with his victory over doubles specialist Mark Woodforde.
Both players struggled with their serve in an uneven opening set, Mantilla holding his twice and Woodforde just once.
While Mantilla managed to gain control of his serve in the second set, Woodforde continued to have problems.
